title: Cabin twin: every physical assumption, in one reviewable file

reviewers: University of Houston, aerospace (life support): CO2 removal assumptions, power budget, operating constraints, alarm thresholds
review.howToReplay: edit a value, keep the file, run `npm run twin:parity` and `npm run plan`; every job manifest records the sha256 of this file, so a result always names the assumptions it was computed with

units.time: minute of story (the board and the video run one story minute per second)

model.reference: packages/host/www/samples/co2-mpc/co2-mpc.js (physicsStep) and packages/dev/tools/co2-mpc/simulate_co2.py in the SpikyPanda repository; the ONNX dynamics model of that sample was trained on the same equations
model.state: co2Ppm (the cabin, well mixed), effectiveRate (the scrubber's first-order lag)
equations: emission = sum over the crew of crew.emissionPerPerson[activity]        [ppm/min]
d(co2Ppm)/dt = emission - removal - leak, clamped to [cabin.floorPpm, cabin.ceilingPpm]
model.states: NOMINAL below thresholds.elevatedPpm; ELEVATED from there to thresholds.criticalPpm; CRITICAL at or above thresholds.criticalPpm

sleep.note: in a sealed volume the ppm rate depends on the cabin volume; the sample folds the volume into these rates

heavy_work.note: the morning exercise of the story uses this level

activities.note: the order is the activity index the graph uses (0 to 3)

initialPpm.note: the story's night 9 starts here; scenario files may override

leakPerMinute.note: fraction of the CO2 lost per minute to leakage; 0 for a perfectly sealed cabin

ceilingPpm.note: numerical ceiling, also the normalisation of the trained dynamics model

preset.note: which of the three presets below the twin uses; the story wants a scrubber at nominal capacity, not oversized

oversized.source: co2-mpc sample, SCRUBBER_PRESETS.oversized (rates[3] = 0.20, tau = 0.3 per minute step)

normal.note: end of life, nominal design capacity

degraded.note: clogged or chemically tired; slower response

rateAtFullCommand.note: fraction of the CO2 excess above the floor removed per minute at full command; the sample's discrete levels (0, 15 %, 40 %, 100 % of this rate) become a continuous command here, linear in the board's speed percent

lagTimeConstantMinutes.source: presets.normal; the sample applies a per-minute step fraction of 0.3, whose continuous equivalent is 1/0.3
lagTimeConstantMinutes.note: chemical activation and gas transport: the scrubber does not reach its rate instantly

removalFloorPpm.note: the absorbent removes CO2 in proportion to the excess above this level

commandToRate.note: rate = rateAtFullCommand * command; the sample's four levels map to 0, 0.15, 0.40 and 1.0 of the full rate, which is not linear in fan speed; a curve can replace this once measured

form.source: the current curve of the bench motor, measured by the factory's fit job
form.note: the shape comes from the real motor on the bench; the scale makes it a habitat scrubber

interceptAmps.source: factory fit on the bench points (specs/bench/scrubber-bench.csv), intercept

slopeAmps.source: factory fit on the bench points, slope

habitatScale.note: 1 W on the bench stands for 300 W in the habitat, so that full command draws about 450 W; the sample's numbers (0, 1, 3, 8 accumulated per minute as Wh) are Wh per minute, i.e. 60 to 480 W, and this scale keeps the same order of magnitude

nominalTargetPpm.note: the level the plan regulates toward; not an alarm

elevatedPpm.note: above this the cabin is ELEVATED: MIN-FLOW forbids any flow below the minimum and any power off

criticalPpm.source: co2-mpc sample, CO2_VITAL, described there as the NASA upper bound for sustained operations
criticalPpm.note: above this the cabin is CRITICAL: the firmware forces full flow and refuses any reduction, whoever asks

floorPercent.source: to be read from the T0 sweep: the lowest command that keeps four resting people below elevatedPpm in steady state
floorPercent.note: the protection floor compiled into the firmware and written in the contract; the agent cannot lower it

otherLoadsW.note: everything that is not the scrubber, held constant; the story says the scrubber is about a third of the life-support power

storyMinutePerBoardSecond.note: the board and the twin integrate the same per-minute equations once per real second; every duration shown in the video is story time

solverStepMinutes.source: the sample integrates with an explicit step of one minute
solverStepMinutes.note: the twin uses the scene's solver at this step for parity with the sample; a smaller step changes the third decimal
